def update(*dicts, **kwargs):
    """Update a dictionary with the key/value pairs from other dictionaries.

    This is a convenience function for the common use case of updating a
    dictionary multiple times.

    ``update(dict1, dict2, dict3)`` is equivalent to
    ``dict1.update(dict2); dict1.update(dict3)``.

    If ``overwrite`` is False (default), the keys from ``kwargs`` will be
    merged into the dictionary, with ``dict`` taking priority. If ``overwrite``
    is True, the keys from ``kwargs`` will overwrite matching keys in
    ``dict``.

    If ``add`` is False (default), the keys from ``kwargs`` will be merged into
    the dictionary, with ``dict`` taking priority. If ``add`` is True, the
    keys from ``kwargs`` will be added to the dictionary, without affecting
    existing keys.

    If ``keep_going`` is False (default), the first dictionary that has a
    given key will be used, and the later dictionaries will be ignored. If
    ``keep_going`` is True, the later dictionaries will overwrite keys from
    earlier dictionaries.

    This function is similar to :func:`dict.update`, but it allows you to
    update a dictionary multiple times, with different strategies.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> d = dict(a=1, b=2)
    >>> update(d, dict(a=3, c=4), dict(b=5, d=6), overwrite=True)
    >>> d
